job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today was an intense day at school. During our sports practice, Rohan tripped and scraped his knee badly. I remembered our first aid lesson and immediately applied firm, direct pressure to the wound using a clean cloth. When the cloth became soaked with blood, I did not remove it; instead, I placed another clean pad directly over the first one to avoid disturbing the clotting process. Later, we saw a student faint from the heat. We made sure he lay flat on his back with his legs slightly elevated to help blood flow to his brain, and we definitely did not try to force water into his mouth while he was unconscious. We also discussed burns in class. My teacher explained that for a minor burn, we should run cool, room-temperature tap water over the area for at least ten minutes. She warned us never to apply ice, as it can damage the skin tissue further. We also learned that for any deep cut, we should wash it gently with clean water rather than scrubbing it harshly, which could cause more damage. It is so important to know these simple steps, as they can prevent serious complications and help someone recover safely until professional medical help arrives.

items.evidence: When the cloth became soaked with blood, I did not remove it; instead, I placed another clean pad directly over the first one to avoid disturbing the clotting process.
items.q: Why was a new pad placed over a blood-soaked cloth instead of replacing it?
options: Taking the cloth off could break the clot
A thicker cloth makes the wound heal faster
The first cloth must be kept as proof
Fresh pads soak up blood better than wet ones
items.explain: Removing the cloth disturbs the clotting process, so a new pad goes on top of the old one.

wrong.why: thinks thickness, not clotting, is the reason
picks an unrelated reason that sounds sensible
thinks a soaked cloth should be swapped for a fresh one

items.q: A student faints in the heat. Which action helps him recover safely?
options: Laying him flat with his legs raised
Keeping him seated with his head held high
Giving him a glass of water to drink
Splashing water on his face to wake him
items.explain: Lying flat with legs raised helps blood reach the brain; water should not be forced into his mouth.

wrong.why: thinks a faint person should stay upright
thinks a fainted person should drink water at once
thinks sprinkling water on the face wakes him

items.evidence: My teacher explained that for a minor burn, we should run cool, room-temperature tap water over the area for at least ten minutes.
items.q: Meena touches a hot pan and gets a small burn. What should she do first?
options: Hold the burn under cool tap water
Press a piece of ice on the burn
Rub the burn with a dry cloth
Cover the burn with a tight bandage
items.explain: A minor burn should be cooled with room-temperature tap water for at least ten minutes.

thinks rubbing helps clean or soothe the skin

It makes the burn heal too slowly
It cools the burn too little to help

items.explain: Ice can damage the skin tissue further, so cool tap water is used instead.
